biggest_gap.what: Nine of the ninety-four quest givers in this build exist anywhere a player can stand, and none of the thirty-five quests behind the '10 of 35' findability headline has a giver in the world at all. QuestEngine.open() has no presence or proximity term, so a quest reports ok in a world containing nobody to say the keyword to.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is round 1's finding moved one layer out. Round 1: the player could not learn the words. Round 2 fixed that properly, with a red control. The player can now learn the words and has nobody to say them to. A rumour in Helstrom teaches 'the upper shelf'; Rootkeeper Jeen, who wants it said, is in no state file in the build.

Then give QuestEngine.open() a presence term, so a quest whose giver is nowhere reports 'blocked: giver absent' instead of ok and every existing instrument inherits the truth.

method_deviations.why: nothing in the tree asks this; QuestEngine.open() has no presence or proximity term, so both round-2 headline instruments certify findability from a gate that cannot know
method_deviations.control: --sabotage assume-present reports presence without asking the world: presence flips 9 -> 94 and talkable stays 9, because talkTo() is attempted for all 94 by record id and only nine succeed. The headline number does not depend on my field matching, which is itself unreliable — listNPCs() does not expose the record id under record/from_record/id.

path_to_ten: (a) Place the quest givers. 85 of 94 are in no state file; put them where their rumours say they are, and add the missing town states (gideon, lilmoth, blackrose, archon) or re-key those 16 rumours to towns that exist. (b) Give QuestEngine.open() a presence term so a quest whose giver is nowhere reports 'blocked: giver absent' instead of ok, and make utility-findability.mjs require a successful H.talkTo(giver) before counting a quest as opened. (c) Raise the 8 disposition_min-0 gates to a value that can refuse somebody, and give Q-MAIN-08 a reserve larger than 0.643 by subtracting the largest npc_disposition consequence the chain can produce at that giver. (d) Re-shape the entry_topics graph so a quest hands you to a different person: at least half the repaired edges should cross a giver, and no bundle of one NPC's quests should form a closed cycle. (e) Give the 102 new infos the filters the system already supports — speaker, race, faction, rank, disposition — so that who is talking changes what you hear. (f) De-duplicate the numbers: 26 free-standing 'eleven's across 20 unrelated records is a tell, and the writing is good enough not to need it.
notes: The round moved real ground: three of round 1's four orphan models are verifiably closed, the topic bootstrap is genuinely repaired with a control that goes red, 40/40 signatures finish penniless and non-violently, and the AR-3 crossing survives a harder test than the builder applied. The writing shipped this round is the best in the tree. The gap is that findability was measured at the gate rather than in the world, and the world is nearly empty of the people the quests name.
